chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from his two brothers, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"Fast upon sighting the crescent and break your fast upon sighting the crescent. The sighting of the crescent is not merely for a man or two men to come and say 'We saw it.' Rather, sighting is when the speaker says 'I saw it,' and the people say 'You are truthful.'
ai.seo_question: What constitutes valid lunar sighting for fasting in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential standard for lunar sighting, emphasizing that the testimony of a single trustworthy individual (*al-qaul bi-qawli al-adl*) suffices for the community to accept the start or end of Ramadan. It distinguishes between mere visual observation and the legal acceptance of testimony, reflecting the Shia reliance on individual credibility (*tawqi*) rather than strict numerical witness requirements found in some other schools. This principle underscores the flexibility and accessibility of Islamic ritual timing based on verified local testimony.
